note: Every withdrawal a person can make that lives outside the tombstone table, which a restore from an older backup would otherwise undo. A restore checkpoint of profile exulanica.restore-tombstone-checkpoint/v2 carries each row this names, and replay writes each one again into the restored database, before any tombstone, by the same statement the product writes: a column kind sets the columns a withdrawal sets on a row whose withdrawal is still open, and an event kind appends the withdrawal's own row. `withdrawn` is the condition a withdrawn row meets; `carried_when` narrows it; `workspace` names the column that says which workspace a row belongs to, or null for a row no workspace owns. A condition with `of` tests a column of the row the carried row names in another table, joined on the `on` columns. An event kind's `ends` names the rows the withdrawal ends, and `order` the column that orders a chain of decisions. `writer` names the product's own writer that writes the carried row, where a row alone is not the whole withdrawal; `continues` names the writer that continues a chain whose restored last decision the carried row cannot follow, because a decision was made after the backup. Both are names of the writers the restore command gives replay (WRITERS in exulanica/orchestration/restore.py); replay refuses, when it starts and before it writes anything, writers other than exactly the names this catalog uses (require_writers in exulanica/deletion/withdrawals.py). `excluded` names every other withdrawal-shaped table or column in the schema and why it is not carried; tests/test_restore_replay_withdrawal_catalog.py fails on any the catalog neither carries nor excludes.

kinds.note: A person withdrawing a claim they made: the retraction row, and assertion.status 'retracted', which the product's retract writes together (exulanica/epistemics/assertions.py). Retracting a name clears the place or person's display name (migration 0002), and a place-name right rests on an active naming claim (0097), so a retraction can end a right. Every row is a retraction; only a retraction of a claim a person stated (kind 'user') is carried. The other writer, a tombstone's cascade (0031), retracts reconstruction_scene_rung_is claims, which only an inference may state, and the replayed tombstone retracts them again.

excluded.reason: A person's identity decision (not them), which undo takes back (exulanica/identity/undo.py). A restore returns it to the backup's state like any other authored edit; it withdraws no permission and no consent.
A confirmed or revoked identity link, an identity decision undo takes back, as for identity_rejection.
The log of identity decisions, derived from them.
A decision about how a place record and an entity relate, which a later decision can reverse. It withdraws no permission and no consent.

assertion.status 'retracted' is the second row of a retraction, written again with it by the retraction kind's writer. A status a tombstone's cascade sets (migrations 0030 and 0031) is written again by the replayed tombstone.
Nothing writes consent_record.revoked_at, and nothing makes a revocation there final.
failure_class 'withdrawn' is written by the recipe withdrawal's own trigger, which replaying the withdrawal runs again.

A state event with basis 'withdrawal' records a tombstone's effect on a place record and names that tombstone; every read of the record asks tombstone_blocks_place_record (migration 0063), which the replayed tombstone answers again.
Written by the cascade of a person's entity tombstone (migration 0030), which replaying the tombstone runs again.
Taking a photograph out of a saved world is an authored edit of that world, not a withdrawal of a permission or a consent; a restore returns a saved world to the backup's state like any other edit.
